newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran president deplores diplomatic row with Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Iran president deplores diplomatic row with Turkey.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Monday deplored a row with neighbouring Turkey that led to tit-for-tat expulsions of diplomats.

"Unfortunately, hidden and visible hands...try now and then to disturb the atmosphere of friendly cooperation between our two countries," Rafsanjani told Turkish envoy Ali Tuygan in remarks broadcast on Tehran radio.

The radio said Tuygan, who arrived in Iran on Saturday, handed Rafsanjani a message from Turkish President Suleyman Demirel in which Demirel expressed regret over the row and called for improved ties.

Rafsanjani welcomed the call and agreed that the two countries should avoid any escalation of the dispute that he said was caused by "certain irresponsible remarks and negative and biased media propaganda".
The row started when Ankara protested to Tehran early in February about comments by Iranian ambassador Mohammad Reza Bagheri at an Islamist rally in the Ankara district of Sincan.
Bagheri's remarks were blasted by Turkish media as a call for the introduction of Islamic sharia law in officially secular but overwhelmingly Moslem Turkey.

A Turkish military commander was quoted last week in the Turkish press as accusing Iran of "terrorism", sparking criticism from Iran's chief consul in the city of Erzurum whom Ankara later declared persona non grata.
Iran said on Saturday it had ordered Turkey's ambassador and another Turkish diplomat in the western city of Orumiyeh to leave.

Diplomatic relations between the 18-year-old Islamic republic and its secularist neighbour have often been strained but the expulsions cap the first major row since an Islamist-led government came to power in Ankara last June.
Turkish foreign ministry spokesman Sermet Atacanli said on Monday Turkey also sought an end to the dispute.
